name: Ivan Chrenko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Ivan Chrenko is Slovakia's first billionaire, who began building his real estate fortune in the early 1990s.
His company, HB Reavis, developed the first business centers in Bratislava and the top shopping mall, later sold.
In one of the earliest big post-Brexit real estate deals in London in 2016,  HB Reavis sold 33 Central to Wells Fargo for a reported $400 million.
In Warsaw, it is constructing one of the tallest buildings in Europe.
He invested more than $10 million in e-commerce cloud startup Exponea, which was sold in 2022.
Chrenko served as CEO of the HB Reavis Group from 1994 to October 2013. He is now the board chairman.

name: Zhao Tao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhao Tao is the chairman of Shandong Buchang Pharmaceuticals, a supplier of traditional Chinese medicine to fight cardiovascular disease.
Zhao received an MBA from Fordham University in New York City.
Buchang started trading on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in November 2016.
Zhao holds a Singapore passport.

name: Christoffel Wiese
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Christoffel Wiese built his Pepkor retail empire by offering bargain prices in South Africa, later expanding into other African countries.
In 2015, South Africa-based furniture retailer Steinhoff International spent $5.7 billion in cash and stock to acquire Pepkor.
He stepped down as Steinhoff chairman in December 2017 after the company disclosed accounting irregularities. Its share price plummeted and Wiese lost his billionaire status.
Wiese regained his 9-figure fortune 2022 when he settled his dispute with Steinhoff for cash and stock, including a 5% stake in Pepkor.
His most valuable asset is Shoprite, but he also holds stakes in real estate firm Collins Property Group, investment holding company Brait and industrial products distributor Invicta Holdings.
In March 2023, Brait spun off food manufacturer Premier Group in an IPO on the Johannesburg stock exchange; Wiese owns about 47% of the shares.
forbes_facts: Wiese's father owned a sheep and cattle farm and a car dealership.
Wiese studied law at Stellenbosch University but switched gears to go into business.

name: Luis Frias
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2018-2020); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Luiz Frias is chairman of PagSeguro Digital, a payments company that went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2018, raising over $2 billion.
Frias' late father acquired one of Brazil's most popular daily newspapers in the 1960s, today known as Folha de S. Paulo.
Group Folha became one of Brazil's largest media conglomerates; Frias joined in 1981, was appointed CEO in 1989 and chairman in 1991.
In 1996, Frias founded UOL, a pioneering Brazilian Internet company, and one of the most visited websites in the country.
PagSeguro Digital is a subsidiary of UOL.

name: Karl Friedrich Braun
name_chinese: 卡尔·弗里德里希·布劳恩
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Karl Friedrich Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
His father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).

A sixth-generation family member, Karl Friedrich is one of three sons of Ludwig Georg.
His sister Anna Maria is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
forbes_facts: Karl Friedrich is a doctor at Berlin's Charit?, with a focus on traumatology.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Hari Bhartia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2021)
forbes_bio: Hari Bhartia co-chairs the Jubilant Bhartia group with interests in energy, fast food, pharma and auto distribution.
The Jubilant group includes four listed companies.
Jubilant Foodworks has hundreds of Domino's Pizza outlets across India.
Jubilant Life Sciences was split into two companies, Jubilant Pharmova and Jubilant Ingrevia. The latter was listed in March 2021.
His older brother Shyam, who is also a billionaire, is co-chairman.
forbes_facts: Hari has a chemical engineering degree from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi.
In December 2024, the Bhartia brothers acquired a 40% stake in Coca Cola's Indian bottler for 125 billion rupees ($1.5 billion).

name: Sun Chengsi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2023-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Sun Chengsi is the chairman of Biwin Storage Technology, a provider of memory and storage products.
He joined the company in 2012, two years after it was set up by four cofounders, including his parents, Sun Rixin and Xu Linxian.
Biwin went public on Shanghai's Star market in 2022.
Its products are used in leading global PC brands such as HP, Lenovo and Acer.

name: Alexander Evnevich
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Alexander Evnevich cofounded Orimi, Russia's largest Russian producer of tea and roasted coffee.
Orimi was founded in 1994 as the Orimi Trade company, which ran wholesale trade of flour, sugar and tea.
The company would become a major player in the Russian tea market, eventually launching its own tea packaging production.
During the 1980s and 1990s, Evnevich worked in Vedeneev VNIIG, the largest scientific center of designing, construction and operation of hydraulic power plants in Russia.
Evnevich's family also controls Maxidom, a large Russian DIY retailer that in 2020 acquired the Russian subsidiary of Castorama, part of British company Kingfisher.

name: Soegiarto Adikoesoemo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Soegiarto Adikoesoemo founded AKR Corporindo as a chemicals trader in 1960 and listed it on the Indonesian Stock Exchange in 1994.
AKR Corporindo is now engaged in petroleum trading and distribution, logistics services, chemical manufacturing and industrial estate.
AKR Corporindo and British oil and gas firm BP's joint venture distributes aviation fuel and  operates jointly branded service stations in Indonesia.
Soegiarto is AKR's president commissioner. His son Haryanto is president director.
In September 2024, AKR's East Java industrial estate JIIPE inaugurated the world's largest single line copper smelter by capacity, run by Indonesia-U.S. joint venture Freeport Indonesia.
forbes_facts: His son Haryanto Adikoesoemo started collecting art over 25 years ago and has accumulated 800 pieces, including works by Andy Warhol and Mark Rothko.
Haryanto opened a museum dedicated entirely to modern and contemporary art, Museum MACAN, in November 2017.

name: Lee Kar Whatt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Lee Kar Whatt is cofounder and managing director of Eco-Shop Marketing, a dollar store chain with more than 400 outlets across Malaysia.
Lee started his career with construction and renovation jobs before setting up his own company in 1994.
He ventured into retail in 2002, and a year later opened the first discount store with his brother Lee Tiong Bin and two other partners.
Creador, a South and Southeast Asia-focused private equity firm, which acquired a 10% stake in Eco-Shop in 2019 for an undisclosed amount, has since sold its shares.
Eco-Shop debuted on Bursa Malaysia in May 2025 after raising RM974 million ($245 million) in the country's largest IPO that year.

name: Yasuhisa Ito
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Yasuhisa Ito is the son of Seven&I Holding's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito and gets his wealth from a minority stake in the global retailing giant.
His two siblings, Junro Ito and Hisako Yamamoto, are also billionaires based on their stakes.
Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.
Seven & i Holdings has 87,000 stores in 19 countries and over $80 billion in annual revenue.
In 2024, Canadian retail giant, Alimentation Couche-Tard made a $47 billion takeover bid for the company but withdrew in July 2025 citing the retailer's lack of cooperation during negotiations.
forbes_facts: The company also runs Denny's restaurants in Japan and owns department stores, supermarkets, and financial services firms.
The family was mulling making a $58 billion management buyout of the company but backed out in February 2025  citing financial issues.
In March 2025, the company announced a massive share buyback plan in a bid to bolster its share price.
In March 2025, Seven & I agreed to sell its York Holdings unit, which includes major supermarket chains and specialty retailers, to Bain Capital for $5.4 billion.

name: Tianqiao Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2003-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Tianqiao is the founder, chairman and CEO of Shanda Investment Group, founded in 1999 by Chen and his family.
Chen is credited with having pioneered and built the online game industry and the online literature industry in China.
Chen stepped down as CEO of Shanda Interactive Entertainment in 2012 and then took the company private.
Chen and his wife Chrissy are active philanthropists, supporting research programs on brain science. Chen commits $1 billion to support global research on the human brain.
Chen cofounded Gestala, China's First Ultrasonic Brain Computer Interface Company in January 2026.
